title: World Cinema Radar — the podcast, Wednesday 4 November 2026

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hello, and welcome to World Cinema Radar, the podcast. I'm {A}, and it's Wednesday the fourth of November.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And I'm {B}. <chuckle> Midweek, and the calendar is doing the talking today. Fewer breaking stories, a lot of dates worth knowing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. Three big things. First, Friday in Spain: fourteen films open at once, and a few of them are really interesting.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Second, the other Fridays of November. We have a first look at what is coming on the thirteenth, the twentieth and the twenty-seventh.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And third, opera. There is a free production online that disappears this weekend. <short pause> So if you like opera, listen to that part.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Everything we say today is in the written edition, with sources and dates. And where sources disagree, we tell you.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Which, honestly, happens twice today. <chuckle> You'll hear it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The Tokyo film festival also closes today. We don't have the winners yet, so we'll leave that for tomorrow.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. Let's start with the cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, Friday the sixth of November. Sensacine counts fourteen releases in Spain. That is a lot for one day.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It is. And it's a mix. Let's pick three. First: Ruega por nosotras, the new film by Daniel Monzón.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I like to say what we know. Our sources say he co-wrote this one with Jorge Guerricaechevarría. |Okay, fair.| The film is set in nineteen seventy-four, in the last years of Franco.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A period drama, then. That is squarely in our taste.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. A nineteen-year-old girl from a wealthy Barcelona family is sent to a strict reformatory in Madrid. It is inspired by a real institution, the Patronato de Protección a la Mujer.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And she makes friends there?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: She befriends a girl called Sole and other inmates. The leads are Zoe Bonafonte and Manuela Calle, and this is Calle's film debut.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It was shown at San Sebastián, out of competition, but we haven't seen it. So no verdict from us.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: No verdict. <short pause> But a historical drama with a social eye. It is on our list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Second: Fiesta Pagäna. This is the biopic of the folk metal band Mägo de Oz, directed by Álvaro Brechner.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Folk metal! I did not have that on my bingo card. <laugh>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Adrián Lastra and Roberto Álamo are in the cast. It premiered at the Morelia festival on the twenty-second of October.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And there is some controversy, right?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes. According to a Mexican outlet, some members of the band oppose the film, and there was legal action against the producer. We looked for the current status and couldn't find it. So we just flag it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Fair enough. Third one is the big one for many people. Godzilla Minus Zero.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Takashi Yamazaki directs again, the same person who made the first one. It is set two years after that film.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And here is our first date problem.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. One Spanish site, Espinof, says the sixth of November in the text, and the ninth in the subtitle. <chuckle> Same article!

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So which one do we trust?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sensacine's calendar, which says the sixth. That is also the date given by the distributor listings we saw. But if you plan to go, check your cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay. And there is a fourth thing on the calendar, which is a bit of a puzzle.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Lee Chang-dong's Possible Love. In Spanish it is Un amor posible.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Sensacine lists it on the sixth. That is also the day it arrives on Netflix, worldwide.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: But Cinemanía says the twenty-third of October for cinemas. And Netflix's own note lists theatrical dates for Korea, Australia, the US, Canada, the UK, Ireland and Japan. Not Spain.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So we don't say there is a Spanish cinema release. <short pause> We say it's on Netflix on Friday, and we say check the listings.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. Better to be careful than to send you to an empty cinema.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And it is a good example of how a release date can mean three different things. A festival date, a cinema date and a streaming date. They are not the same.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Never the same. <chuckle> We keep a rule on the Radar: we never deduce a Spanish date from a date in another country. Korea, the US, Japan, all different.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So for Possible Love, the safe sentence is: Netflix, Friday the sixth, in Spain and everywhere else. That we can say, because Netflix says it.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Good. And the film itself runs for almost three hours, so plan an evening.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me add something about the way we read these things. A calendar tells you a date. It does not tell you if the film is good.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Very true. <chuckle> And a trailer tells you even less. So when we say a film is interesting, we mean it fits what we like, not that it is good.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Exactly. For Ruega por nosotras that means history, a period setting and a story about young women. For Fiesta Pagäna it means a curious subject and a loud soundtrack, I imagine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: |Loud, yes.| And for Godzilla Minus Zero it means a big Japanese film in a very big week. Japan, cinema, spectacle. We like that mix.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: If you only go to the cinema once this month, which would you pick?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Honestly? I would look at the other Fridays first. <short pause> This one is crowded, and the thirteenth and the twentieth have names I want to wait for.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is a fair plan. Fourteen releases in one day also means some of them will have very few screens, so check early.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One more honest note. Sacamantecas is also in the list, and we talked about it a few days ago. So it is still the same date, the sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now a quick look ahead. Sensacine already lists the next three Fridays. We want to be clear: this is only a calendar. We haven't checked synopses or casts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. So these are names and directors, nothing more. Friday the thirteenth first.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And what a title for a horror fan: Victorian Psycho, directed by Zachary Wigon.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: <chuckle> Friday the thirteenth and a Victorian psycho. Somebody planned that. I'm just saying.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Also on the thirteenth, Martin McDonagh's Wild Horse Nine.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: McDonagh is always worth watching. We know nothing more about this one, so let's not guess.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then Ti West has a film called Scrooge y los fantasmas de la Navidad. That is the Spanish title.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And David Leitch, Cómo robar un banco. Plus Jaleos, by the Catalan director Isaki Lacuesta.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Before the twentieth, one more thought on the thirteenth. If you like your cinema dark, that week is for you.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Dark and varied. A Victorian horror title, and a Christmas ghost story, judging by the Spanish title.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: I like that. A ghost story near Christmas is a very old tradition.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It is. But, again, we only know the title and the director, so we won't promise anything about the tone.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay. The twentieth. This is the big Hollywood Friday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping, by Francis Lawrence. In Spain it is Amanecer en la cosecha.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: But the one I want to see is Moulin, by László Nemes.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We only have the calendar entry for it, so no details. But the name alone makes us curious.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Also on the twentieth, Jane Schoenbrun's Adolescencia, sexo y muerte en Campamento Miasma.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which is a very long title. <laugh> And it has a Spanish comedy neighbour, Citas: La película, by Gemma Ferraté.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And then the twenty-seventh. Hermanas, by Ione Hernández. And El director, by Dani de la Orden.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And here comes our second correction. Sanguine, the French body horror that won at Sitges.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. We were not sure whether it opens on the sixth or the twenty-seventh. Different sites said different things.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sensacine says the twenty-seventh, so that is the date we use for now.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Notice something about this list. It is quite varied. A Hollywood franchise, a historical film from Nemes, a Spanish drama, a comedy, a horror.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And Spanish cinema is well represented. Lacuesta, Hernández, de la Orden, Ferraté. Four Spanish names in three weeks.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That is good for a reader in Catalonia. Though we have not checked the languages or the versions, so Catalan screenings are a question for your cinema.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. We prefer to say that than to guess. <short pause> Back to the calendar.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good. So you don't have to rush this Friday for that one. <short pause> The rest of the details are in the edition, and we will confirm each date before the Friday.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Now let's go to the stage. And this is a practical one. OperaVision, the free online opera platform, has an opera marked as last chance to watch.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Which one?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Le Roi d'Ys, from the Opéra national du Rhin. The production is by Oliver Py, and Samy Rachid conducts.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: When does it expire?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: According to OperaWire, it went online on the eighth of May and expires on the eighth of November. That is this Sunday. The recording is from March this year.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Let me say what the recording is, as far as we know. A production from the Opéra national du Rhin, filmed in March, with five named singers in the cast.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Five names on the list we saw, but I will not read them out. They are in the written edition, and I would certainly say them wrong. <chuckle>

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. French names, with all those vowels. The edition has them spelled properly.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Free, and for a few more days. <short pause> That is worth knowing.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: We haven't watched it, and we don't have a full cast list in front of us, so we say that plainly. But the platform is official and free.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And there are other expiries, right?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: OperaWire's May article lists three more, each six months after release. Medusa, a modern opera by Iain Bell, at La Monnaie in Brussels, on the fifteenth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Then Così fan tutte from the Hungarian State Opera on the twenty-third. And Ponchielli's I Lituani, from Vilnius, on the twenty-ninth.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Now, here is the caveat. We looked at OperaVision's front page and didn't find those three there.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So maybe they're hidden, or maybe the dates changed. <sigh> Please check before you plan your weekend around them.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Exactly. What the site does announce for November is this: De Materie on the sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: We mentioned it a few days ago.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then Šárka, from the National Theatre in Brno, on the fifteenth. And Peter Grimes, from the Finnish National Opera, on the twenty-sixth.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Peter Grimes. That one is for me.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: <chuckle> I knew it. There is also a gala of the International Opera Awards on the twenty-first, and two family titles on the twenty-second.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let me say why this matters. Opera on a stage is a big, expensive thing. Having it free at home is a real gift.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And the catch is the time limit. Many of these streams stay up for six months, then they are gone. So it is a bit like a festival: you have a window.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A window, yes. Think of Le Roi d'Ys as a small event with a closing date on Sunday.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: It also fits our rule for the stage section: we look for complete recordings, not trailers or short clips. This is a complete production, as far as the platform says.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: As far as the platform says. <chuckle> We say that a lot today. But we want to be accurate.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: One more thing: the platform lists a gala for the International Opera Awards. That is an event, not a staged opera, so it is a different kind of viewing.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Right. Nice to watch, but not the same as a full production.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And one last point. We don't know how long the new ones stay up. The platform doesn't say. So if you see something you like, don't wait too long.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's put the dates in order. Today, Wednesday the fourth: the Tokyo festival closes. We haven't found the winners yet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Friday the sixth, in Spain: the fourteen releases. Ruega por nosotras, Fiesta Pagäna, Godzilla Minus Zero and Sacamantecas, among others.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The same day, Possible Love on Netflix, and De Materie on OperaVision.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Then Sunday the eighth: Le Roi d'Ys leaves OperaVision.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Friday the thirteenth: McDonagh, Ti West and David Leitch, in Spanish cinemas.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Sunday the fifteenth: Šárka arrives on OperaVision, and Medusa should expire, according to OperaWire.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Friday the twentieth: The Hunger Games and Moulin. Saturday the twenty-first: the Opera Awards gala.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thursday the twenty-sixth: Peter Grimes. And Friday the twenty-seventh: Sanguine and Hermanas.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: A tip. Put the sixth, the eighth and the thirteenth in your own calendar. Those are the three with a real deadline or a real choice.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The sixth, because there is so much. The eighth, because of the opera. And the thirteenth, because of the horror.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And if the Tokyo winners are announced later today, we will tell you tomorrow. We would rather wait for the official list.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: All the cinema dates are for Spain, from Sensacine. Other countries are different, so don't mix them up.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Time for our picks. Remember, the affinity score is ours. It is not a critics' score and not an audience score.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Right. First, Possible Love, by Lee Chang-dong. Affinity four out of five, medium confidence.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: He comes back eight years after Burning. It is a long drama, one hundred and sixty-four minutes, and Cinemanía says it won at Venice.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: On Netflix on Friday. We haven't seen it, so that is all from reading.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Second: Ruega por nosotras. Affinity three out of five, low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Low, because we only know the synopsis and credits. But a period drama about reformatories in Franco's Spain is a good fit for the profile.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And third, the opera. Le Roi d'Ys on OperaVision. Affinity three, low confidence.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Free, and gone on Sunday. We don't have the full cast, which is why the confidence is low.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And a word about how we choose. Our affinity score looks at what the reader likes: period drama, horror, clever comedy, international cinema, and filmed theatre and opera.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: So a film can be very good and still get a three from us. <laugh> That is not an insult.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Not at all. It means we are being honest about taste and honest about what we have seen, which is nothing yet.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: The full list is in the edition. And if you only have time for one thing this week?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: For me, Possible Love. <short pause> It is a weekend with a lot of choices.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So, the idea of the day. Friday is crowded in Spanish cinemas, and one free opera is about to disappear.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And we dropped a few stories we could not read properly. Fewer items, but checked. <chuckle> That's our rule.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: One practical thing for tomorrow: we will look for the Tokyo winners, and we will check again the Friday releases.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: And if a date changes, we will say it, and we will say what changed. Not just the new date.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks for listening. See you tomorrow on the Radar.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: See you tomorrow.

pronunciations.Patronato de Protección a la Mujer: Pah-troh-nah-toh deh Pro-tek-thyon ah lah Moo-her
pronunciations.Scrooge y los fantasmas de la Navidad: Skroodj ee los fan-tahs-mahs deh lah Nah-vee-dad
pronunciations.Adolescencia, sexo y muerte en Campament: Ah-doh-les-then-thyah, sek-soh ee mwer-teh en Kam-pah-men-toh Mee-as-mah
